speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are having trouble sleeping and waking up frightened; can you tell me exactly what these episodes look like and if anyone else in the room is affected?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description; you mentioned she yells and cries but is not confused afterward—does she have any memory of the events that occur during these frightened awakenings? Additionally, are these episodes accompanied by any rapid breathing, sweating, or a sudden racing heart before she becomes scared?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. The presence of detailed recall of bad dreams, crying/yelling during episodes, and normal orientation immediately upon waking distinguishes this from sleep terrors, which typically involve amnesia and confusion. The fatigue the next day and bedtime procrastination are consistent with this diagnosis.
